topic: Const Member Functions and const_cast Usage
explanation: In C++, member functions can be declared as 'const' to indicate that they do not modify the state of the object. This allows such functions to be called on const instances of classes. Additionally, when a const member function needs to return a non-const pointer or reference to internal data, it can use 'const_cast' to remove the const qualifier, enabling controlled access to internal mutable members. This pattern is useful for providing read-only access to internal resources while maintaining const-correctness in interface design.
